name: merge-identity
description: Non-destructive identity consolidation (§11). The merged-away Concept stays addressable and keeps forwarding; the history that referenced it keeps referencing it (§11.2); ordinary new writes land on the identity that survived (§11.3); and no merge may make canonical resolution — following `merged_into` to its fixpoint — cycle (§11.1).

cases.name: the merged-away Concept keeps its own name and leaves ordinary recall
it forwards to the identity that survived
history keeps referring to what it referred to
cases.command: FIND(?raw.key) WHERE { ?p PROPOSITION (?s, "prefers", ?o) ?raw CONCEPT {id: ?stored, state: ?state} FILTER(?stored == ?p.subject.id) }

cases.name: two post-merge writes resolve to one canonical Proposition on the survivor
re-sending the same merge is a no_effect, not a conflict
merging back would make canonical resolution cycle
merging a Concept into itself has no effect

Option.description: A preference option used by these fixtures. A real Space types each option by its kind (Profile §5.5, §7), because prefers partitions by the option's Concept Type; one catch-all type is one partition.
